episode_title: How do you ensure Integrity & Security within AI? w/ Chiru Bhavansikar, Arhasi AI

real_qa.q: What is the difference between Large Language Models and AI agents in enterprise AI applications?
real_qa.r: LLMs are comparable to the brain of a human being—mandatory and required to function. AI agents, however, expand possibilities beyond generative AI by encompassing LLMs with deep learning and statistical modeling in a seamless fashion. AI agents bring LLMs close to the business, make them functional, and create business impact by executing tasks autonomously, optimizing business processes, reducing costs, and improving productivity—something LLMs alone cannot achieve.
real_qa.requete: AI agents vs LLMs difference business impact

real_qa.q: What are the best practices for securing AI agents against emerging threats in enterprise environments?
real_qa.r: Best practices include implementing traditional IAM (Integrated Access Management) controls and establishing trusted boundaries around AI agents regarding network access, resources, and data. Organizations should establish contextual guardrails limiting agents to their relevant domain (e.g., supply chain agents should not access manufacturing data). Sensitive data protection must be enforced in real time during model decision-making and communication, not just during training. Data loss protection and continuous monitoring are mandatory.
real_qa.requete: AI agents security best practices IAM guardrails

real_qa.q: How can organizations address bias in AI agent training and deployment?
real_qa.r: Traditional data science methodologies including feature engineering and proper data preparation remain applicable and are not redundant in artificial intelligence. Organizations must ensure the data consumed by AI agents does not contain bias. Beyond data preparation, implement monitoring systems that measure bias and report on it, and deploy models that can detect and redact bias when it appears. This creates a checks-and-balances governance model similar to how countries manage oversight.
real_qa.requete: AI agent bias detection data preparation feature engineering

real_qa.q: How should organizations adapt to evolving AI regulations like EU AI Act, Australian regulation, and US White House executive order?
real_qa.r: Organizations should identify common patterns across different regulatory frameworks (EU regulation, Australian regulation, Japanese regulation, US White House executive order) and translate those into policies that feed into a system which continuously watches and observes adherence to those policies. When drift is detected, the system points out specific policy violations. However, many regulations cannot be technologically solved alone—people and process aspects require regular audits and assessments to prove compliance.
real_qa.requete: EU AI Act Australian regulation compliance automation

real_qa.q: How can AI be used to create visibility into shadow AI usage and resource consumption within organizations?
real_qa.r: Organizations can use AI itself to solve the shadow AI problem by creating visibility into effective usage of technical and storage resources across the organization. AI can map resource usage and create integrated views where security tools (such as SIM, Splunk, and other security systems) previously provided disconnected views. This approach enables root cause analysis of security incidents to complete in days rather than months.
real_qa.requete: shadow AI visibility SIEM Splunk security incident analysis
